title: The Quality of Accruals and Earnings: The Role of Accrual Estimation Errors
summary: All three CFO slopes retain their signs and strong significance. Magnitudes and fit differ: lag/current/lead CFO 0.143/-0.548/0.122 versus 0.17/-0.62/0.09; mean adjusted R2 0.447 versus 0.47.
sample: 14,346 firm-years and 1,465 firm regressions versus 15,234 and 1,725.
caveat: Firm-specific OLS and CFO denominator/lead-lag screening interpretations; historical population not recovered.

title: Real and Accrual-Based Earnings Management in the Pre- and Post-Sarbanes-Oxley Periods
summary: All seven SOX coefficients reverse the published sign; time/SCA effects are generally much weaker. None of the seven rows is numerically close at published precision.
sample: 93,508 common firm-years versus 87,217 paper-wide; published model-specific N unavailable.
caveat: Extreme tails and small asset denominators dominate local moments; the paper does not specify trimming or the RM standardization population. Source test sidedness is unknown.

title: Cash Flow Patterns as a Proxy for Firm Life Cycle
summary: Cash-flow stage contrasts retain their negative significant pattern; age contrasts retain signs/significance, but some total stage levels change sign. A&R loses the three published significant stage contrasts.
caveat: Legacy IINT replaced by unverified IDIT proxy; source estimator unspecified; CF and A&R require the installed covariance adjustment.

title: Exploring the Term of the Auditor-Client Relationship and the Quality of Earnings: A Case for Mandatory Auditor Rotation?
summary: Of five executed scopes, absolute current accruals and positive current accruals retain negative significant tenure effects; raw current accruals remain negative/nonsignificant. Absolute DA loses significance, raw DA changes from positive/significant to negative/nonsignificant. Three signed truncated regressions are blocked.
sample: Main N 27,414 versus 41,250; signed subsets differ separately.
caveat: Historical auditor/M&A coverage and cash mapping differ; three native truncated-MLE convergence failures.

title: The Mispricing of Abnormal Accruals
summary: Forecast and valuation slope directions retain the source pattern. CFO and ABNAC pricing equality rejections persist; NAC equality changes from p<0.001 to p=0.1624. All-component and within-equation joint rejections persist.
caveat: Conditional Gaussian likelihood with independent equation errors is an explicit identification approximation to the source's unspecified GLS/weighted-SSR method.

title: Accruals and the Prediction of Future Cash Flows
summary: All seven primary cash-flow component slopes retain signs and significance, with appreciably smaller DEPR and AMORT. All seven earnings benchmarks retain positive significant current earnings. In k=6, lag-5 significance is lost and lag-6 becomes significant under conventional two-sided interpretation of the published t values.
caveat: Unspecified source tail convention and percentile details; higher-lag discrepancies are supporting-model results.

title: The Role of Accounting Conservatism in Mitigating Bondholder-Shareholder Conflicts over Dividend Policy and in Reducing Debt Costs
summary: Market-conservatism model retains all three positive significant interest terms. Accounting-conservatism DIV loses significance (0.115, p=.466 versus .404, p=.001); LEV remains nonsignificant with a small sign change.
sample: Both local models N 140 versus 704 and 632.
caveat: Severe R&D/advertising coverage loss, legacy rating/depreciation proxies; source predicted tests are one-tailed and exports are two-tailed.

title: Does Income Smoothing Improve Earnings Informativeness?
summary: Both smoothing interactions remain positive and significant: .8120/.3759 versus .681/.308; magnitudes are larger locally.
caveat: Source covariance and price/return-date details unspecified; narrower local return/EPS spreads.

title: The Persistence and Pricing of Earnings, Accruals, and Cash Flows When Firms Have Large Book-Tax Differences
summary: Both large-BTD persistence interactions remain negative/significant, -.0904/-.2239 versus -.100/-.212; their equality is rejected in both. The local intercept becomes significant.
caveat: Broader source missing-variable screen not fully recoverable; unknown TLCF/current-tax statuses retained according to stated screen.

title: Accrued Earnings and Growth: Implications for Future Profitability and Market Mispricing
summary: GrLTNOA and ACC retain negative significant slopes, but their equality is rejected locally (p=.00001554) versus nonrejection in the paper (p=.11). Adjusted R2 .624 versus .62.
caveat: Goodwill legacy-item proxy, missing accounting-change footnote detail, and unresolved population difference.

title: Earnings Management: New Evidence Based on Deferred Tax Expense
summary: Eight of nine models execute. Most DTE patterns persist; Table 2 target-3 total accruals lose significance (.732 versus .0422), and Table 4 target-1 DTE gains significance (.025 versus .1157). Some nonsignificant accrual coefficients reverse sign; Table 2 target 2 is blocked.
caveat: Published one-tailed wording conflicts with table labeling; exports are two-sided. IBES split screen unavailable and linkage is approximate.

title: A Temporal Analysis of Quarterly Earnings Thresholds: Propensities and Valuation Consequences
summary: All three trends retain negative slopes. Negative-surprise trend remains strongly significant; loss/decrease trends remain nonsignificant at 5% using two-sided t interpretation. Local decrease p=.081 matters at 10%. Chow rejection persists.
sample: 18 annual observations per regression; underlying observations differ from the paper.
caveat: Exact split-adjusted primary construction unavailable; these are documented approximation results, not an exact baseline replication.

title: The Use of DuPont Analysis by Market Participants
summary: Published positive delta-ATO association is absent in all three models. Table 5 delta-ATO and future ATO turn negative/nonsignificant; Table 8 delta-PM becomes significant. SUR remains positive/significant.
sample: 25,469 common observations versus reported all-tests-common 38,716; 19 annual fits.
caveat: Unassigned tests not rebuilt for source common sample; Newey-West lag 1 is assumed and source covariance wording conflicts.

title: Measuring Reporting Conservatism
summary: The one reported focal interaction is positive, .2837306 versus .302 (-6.0%); local p<.001. Source supplies no comparable inference for that estimate.
caveat: Other source coefficients and focal standard error/test unavailable; direction/magnitude comparison only.

title: Are Selling, General, and Administrative Costs “Sticky”?
summary: Stickiness remains negative and strongly significant, but interaction magnitude is about 69.5% smaller: -.05844 versus -.1914. Sales slope .5813 versus .5459.
caveat: Historical source population and item-number mapping unresolved; qualitative agreement does not imply a close numerical match.

title: The Role of Accruals in Asymmetrically Timely Gain and Loss Recognition
summary: All 48 scopes execute. Most book/return interactions preserve positive significance; Table 3 book effects are often much larger. Table 5D SIC3 industry-adjusted interactions reverse all three published negative signs, with other joint-model inference changes.
sample: Table 3A pooled CF/DD/Jones: 78,963/66,210/75,590 versus 57,362/46,821/54,838. Separate industry counts and all other scopes documented in review.
caveat: Joint Table 5D is multicollinear per source; historical populations and several scaling/median/trim conventions unspecified.

title: A Temporal Analysis of Earnings Surprises: Profits versus Losses
summary: All nine annual trend slopes retain source direction and significance; magnitudes and annual frequencies/medians differ.
sample: 16 annual observations per trend; 190,006 underlying events versus 176,519.
caveat: Fiscal-year proxy and adjusted IBES vintage; source regression covariance unspecified.

title: The Impact of Financial Reporting Quality on Debt Contracting: Evidence from Internal Control Weakness Reports
summary: Financial-covenant effects lose significance; both secured-probit effects reverse from positive to negative; interest-rate uncorrected effect also reverses and loses significance. PP uncorrected effect stays negative/significant. Other outcomes have mixed nonsignificant signs.
sample: Main 223 versus 2,828; secured 212; general covenants 37; PP probit 88 versus 2,045.
caveat: Severe borrower/rating linkage loss and small-cluster/separation limits; not an equivalent source population.

title: Biases and Lags in Book Value and Their Effects on the Ability of the Book-to-Market Ratio to Predict Book Return on Equity
summary: Five benchmark models retain negative BTM and positive ROE slopes. Five decomposition models differ in time effects and bias-minus-lag contrasts; horizon-3 incremental test is nonsignificant (.064) unlike source.
sample: 4,409 versus 6,044 in each of ten fits.
caveat: Robust Wald is not source classical partial F; common-income and primary-share market-value proxies; historical PST returns unavailable.

title: Performance matched discretionary accrual measures
summary: Six residual-generating regression families have no direct published coefficient target. Their Table 1 residual distributions differ: Jones SD 14.65% versus 9.98%, with generally wider local residual and matched-residual distributions.
caveat: These are descriptive-distribution comparisons, not baseline coefficient or hypothesis-test matches.

title: Earnings Management through Real Activities Manipulation
summary: All three suspect-firm signs agree. Discretionary-expense and production effects remain significant; abnormal CFO is -.01295, p=.056 versus -.0200, t=-3.05, losing conventional two-sided 5% significance.
caveat: Newey-West bandwidth assumed; source discretion-expense wording conflicts. Review statement about unchanged significance refers to A3-to-A4, not source agreement.

title: Accrual-Based and Real Earnings Management Activities Around Seasoned Equity Offerings
summary: None of six published negative significant focal findings survives at two-sided 5%: DA/CFO/RM1/RM2 lose significance, production reverses sign, and DISX reverses to positive/significant (p=.045). RM1 remains marginal at 10% (p=.093).
sample: 2,030 local model observations; published Table 6 N unavailable. Paper-wide offers 1,511 versus 2,070 local.
caveat: SDC categories and matching/event-year rules approximate. Corrects review prose saying RM1 was insignificant at 10%; its printed .093 is below .10.

title: Accrual reliability, earnings persistence and stock prices
summary: All seven accrual-component directions and significance patterns agree: six negative/significant and DSTI positive/nonsignificant. ROA .8099 versus .801; adjusted R2 .637 versus .595.
caveat: Historical population/SIC/link choices unresolved; source descriptive winsorization status unstated. A2 reuses unchanged A1 construction and independently reruns Stata.

title: Discretionary-accruals models and audit qualifications
summary: All four DA slopes stay positive; both time-series models remain nonsignificant at 5%, both cross-sectional models significant. All coefficient magnitudes are smaller locally.
caveat: Source one-sided comparisons checked separately from two-sided exports; qualification population, Big Six crosswalk, and matching conventions unresolved.

title: Do investors overvalue firms with bloated balance sheets?
summary: All six focal accrual/NOA signs and 5% inference decisions agree across three panels. Panel B NOA is more negative (-.004429 versus -.0023); several other estimates are close.
sample: 438 monthly fits each; 1,174,665/1,153,631/1,122,680 local firm-months. Comparable source firm-month N not reported.
caveat: Historical information timing and raw-return/FX conventions remain assumptions.

title: Earnings volatility and earnings predictability
summary: All 21 earnings-persistence slopes stay positive/significant and the lower persistence at high volatility survives. Q1-Q5 slope and adjusted-R2 contrasts retain rejection, although magnitudes and R2 often differ substantially.
sample: Full sample 26,236 versus 22,113; exploratory 13,175 versus 11,061. Fit-specific Ns differ by horizon/quintile.
caveat: Original split seed unknown; required early OANCF coverage missing, so local complete history excludes target 1988–1990. Simulation tail 0/1,000 is finite-resolution evidence.

title: Asymmetric timeliness of earnings, market-to-book and conservatism in financial reporting
summary: All eight b1/g1 level sign-and-significance patterns agree, but historical j=4 combined bad-news slope gains significance. Several adjacent-horizon tests change decisions, including future k2-k1 g1 and k3-k2 b1.
caveat: Source contains sign/decimal typos; reviewed original tables/prose control. Tests of level, sum, and change are distinct.

title: The implied cost of capital: A new approach
summary: Earnings slopes retain positive significance in all three horizons; accruals remain negative, but horizon 3 loses 5% significance. Dividend dummy gains significance in all horizons; negative-earnings dummy loses 5% significance in the first two.
sample: 41 rolling fits per horizon; overlapping local training-row Ns are not comparable to source forecast-coverage counts.
caveat: Newey-West lag 3 and training-window interpretation assumed; installed lag covariance supports individual tests, not a full joint HAC test.

title: Financial reporting quality and idiosyncratic return volatility
summary: Both TIME x earnings-quality effects remain positive and significant at 1%; DD .005814 versus .017 and ABACC2 .009598 versus .012. DD magnitude is much smaller.
caveat: Severe sample shortfall; unspecified GMM instruments replaced by RHS self-instruments, producing OLS point estimates with panel HAC inference.

title: Tax‐Avoidance Activities of U.S. Multinational Corporations*
summary: MNC reverses from -.0633 to +.3265 (local p=.004); its SIZE/PTI interactions also reverse and lose significance. Most other published focal effects are absent.
sample: 182 versus 16,750; only 38 local domestic and 144 multinational observations.
caveat: Severe geographic-segment and MNC-status coverage/semantic limits; source mixes one-sided and two-sided tests.

title: The Relation between Analysts' Forecasts of Long‐Term Earnings Growth and Stock Price Performance Following Equity Offerings*
summary: The two-equation system gives market-efficiency p=.0601 versus .001, and naive-expectations p=5.50e-20 versus .516. Valuation alpha1 reverses from +.138/nonsignificant to -.7245/significant.
caveat: Independent-error conditional Gaussian likelihood is an identification approximation to unspecified source WLS; source growth-start date conflicts.

title: Financial Statement Comparability and the Efficiency of Acquisition Decisions
summary: All three target-comparability findings lose significance. ACQ_CAR reverses sign: -.005 (p=.616) versus +.017; synergy .003 (p=.753) versus .018; delta-ROA .010 (p=.313) versus .025.
caveat: Source focal inference one-sided; even corresponding expected-direction tests do not restore significance. Deal-value proxy and comparability coverage remain limits. Uses final A2, not earlier A1 counts.

title: Capitalization versus Expensing: Evidence on the Uncertainty of Future Earnings from Capital Expenditures versus R&D Outlays
summary: R&D and CapEx/PPE effects remain positive/significant in all three models, with larger R&D slopes. Local coefficients are often two to four times published magnitudes.
caveat: Large sample shortfall, advertising availability, and share/asset-timing source ambiguities; numerical match not achieved.

title: The Predictive Value of Expenses Excluded from Pro Forma Earnings
summary: All 12 model scopes preserve focal signs and inference: total/other exclusions negative/significant; CFO special items nonsignificant, FCF special items positive/significant. FCF total coefficients are materially more negative.
sample: Local Ns range 133,147–172,513; source reports parent N 143,462 but no like-for-like horizon-specific regression Ns.
caveat: IBES basic/diluted actual flag missing; cash-flow mappings and split bases approximate; printed variance formula differs from standard package formula.

title: Using Asset Turnover and Profit Margin to Forecast Changes in Profitability
summary: Weighted delta-ATO remains positive/significant and delta-PM nonsignificant. Published NOA-growth and ATO x PM interaction effects disappear (local p=.458/.905).
caveat: Unspecified source estimator/covariance; extreme NOA-growth tail retained because no direct source cutoff exists.

title: The persistence of earnings and cash flows and the role of special items: Implications for the accrual anomaly
summary: Both models retain negative significant low-accrual and special-item interactions and positive persistence slopes. Adjusted R2 .491/.478 versus .374/.359; magnitudes differ.
caveat: Source and template use different star legends; inference comparison uses the stated thresholds, not star counts.

title: Asymmetric timeliness tests of accounting conservatism
summary: All four actual/simulated good/bad-news slopes remain positive/significant, with much stronger bad-news slopes. Simulated good-news magnitude differs (.035 versus .009) and exceeds the local actual-good-news slope, reversing that point-estimate ordering.
caveat: Original simulation seed unknown; only the retained single-draw regressions are assessed, not an equivalence test or repeated-simulation result.

title: Separating Winners from Losers among LowBook-to-Market Stocks using Financial Statement Analysis
summary: The focal GSCORE effect loses significance: .0134, p=.124 versus .034, t=5.53. Separate Bernard-adjusted t=1.573 is also nonsignificant.
caveat: Large signal missingness and raw-expense availability losses; source variable-description conflicts and covariance approximation.

title: Comparing the Value Relevance of Two Operating Income Measures
summary: All four regressions run, but STREET-versus-EPSOP slope and adjusted-R2 rankings reverse in both valuation and information tables. STREET slope 2.297 versus 19.28; STREET ERC .01825 versus 1.3451.
sample: 48,306 versus 22,024 for valuation; 33,602 versus 22,092 for information.
caveat: Paired slope/Vuong tests were not reproduced; separate p-values cannot establish paired inference. Unresolved IBES EPS basis and extreme STREET tails.

title: What do dividends tell us about earnings quality?
summary: None of six dividend-persistence interactions is significant at 5% locally, versus five positive/significant source effects. Three local signs reverse; the latest h1 slope is negative and marginal at 10%.
caveat: IDIT coverage and historical incorporation/FX limits; their contribution to the entire discrepancy is not established.

title: Excess Returns to R&D-Intensive Firms
summary: All three R&D/ARNOA rank slopes remain positive and strongly significant: .102/.262/.464 versus .073/.168/.421; local magnitudes are larger.
sample: 24,922 regression observations; comparable published regression N not reported (35,841 is a parent count).
caveat: Source estimator/covariance and some denominator timing unspecified; no exact numerical match claimed.

title: Has goodwill accounting gone bad?
summary: Both post-142 models retain positive significant IMPI and BTMG1. Pre-142 IMPI gains significance (.256, p=.040 versus .162, z=1.24). Pseudo-R2 is higher in all models.
sample: Conditional Ns 2,325/9,973/9,140; published Table 1 counts are parent populations, not comparable conditional-fit Ns.
caveat: Firm strata are assumed because source conditional-logit strata are unspecified; conditional selection is substantial.

title: An Alternative Interpretation of the Discontinuity in Earnings Distributions
summary: Both models retain the regional slope pattern and both equality rejections. Adjusted R2 falls from .99/.99 to .926/.864; F statistics and several slopes differ substantially.
caveat: Source extra-outlier deletion unspecified; 8,666 unresolved industry classifications retained. Common local sample differs from source panel-specific samples.

title: Evaluating cross-sectional forecasting models for implied cost of capital
summary: Nine forecasting scopes run. HVZ earnings slopes/R2 are relatively close but horizon-3 dividend-dummy significance is lost. EP signs/inference persist with large magnitude gaps. RI TACC reverses at h1/h2 and loses significance at h2/h3.
sample: 44 annual vectors except RI h3 with 43 identified vectors; source fit-row Ns not reported.
caveat: First RI h3 annual fit rank deficient; missing-accrual zero rule extended to FX-only construction gaps, explicitly approximate.

title: Corporate tax avoidance: data truncation and loss firms
summary: The time trend becomes positive/significant: .000244, t=2.25, p=.0335 versus .0001, t=1.15. Effect is about 2.44 times the source estimate.
caveat: Historical entity flags and finite-sample two-way covariance choices are approximate; broader descriptive populations are not regression-sample targets.

title: Does the Stock Market Fully Appreciate the Implications of Leading Indicators for Future Earnings? Evidence from Order Backlog
summary: The joint system fails to reject backlog pricing equality (p=.9631 versus source p<.001). Earnings-pricing equality is rejected at .0366 versus published .05; focal backlog conclusion does not survive this construction.
caveat: Approximate size-return benchmark and independent-error conditional Gaussian estimator; not a like-for-like rejection of the original study.

title: Analyst Forecasting Ability and the Stock Price Reaction to Forecast Revisions
summary: Superior analyst slope loses significance (.0866, p=.213 versus .2355, t=3.957); normal slope rises to .2384 versus .0890. Superior-normal and superior-inferior equality tests lose 5% rejection (.0784/.5279 versus .025/.015).
caveat: Large overlapping-event exclusions, consensus/availability conventions, and return benchmark/covariance approximations; normal-versus-inferior remains nonsignificant.
